commit.message:
fix(umi): AnnotateBamWithUmis should not fail on UMIs without BAM records (#1171)

With --sorted, a UMI in the FASTQ with no corresponding BAM records was
counted as a missing UMI and caused a non-zero exit, contradicting the
documented behavior.  This is the common case when an upstream tool
discards read pairs, so it is now counted and logged separately, but is
not an error.

This restores the behavior of #735, which was reverted by #657 while
retaining its documentation; the guard added in #1055 only covered extra
FASTQ records at the end of the file, not in the middle.

Two related fixes:

  - BAM records left over once the FASTQ is exhausted are now written out
    un-annotated.  Previously the FASTQ was consumed looking for a match,
    then execution failed before the writer was closed, truncating the
    output BAM to zero records.
  - Failures now report the number of BAM records without a UMI and exit
    1, rather than exiting with that count, which exited 0 when the count
    was a multiple of 256.

As a result --fail-fast no longer triggers on a UMI without BAM records,
and in sorted mode now names the read it failed on rather than reporting
that the FASTQ was exhausted.

The tests for extra FASTQ records were vacuous from #735 until #1047 as
they never called execute(), which is how #657 reverted the fix with CI
green; they only covered extra records at the end of the FASTQ once
re-enabled in #1055.  They now cover extra records mid-FASTQ, and assert
that all records are written whether or not they were annotated.  FASTQ
fixtures are built from FastqRecord rather than raw lines so record
boundaries are no longer expressed as line counts, and --fail-fast, which
had no coverage at all, is now tested in both modes.
